42 nomad visas in the registry. The lowest threshold is not worth taking at face value

The private registry WhereNext, as of September 23, 2026, holds 42 programs for remote workers. Additionally, in the same database, there are 24 pension routes, 28 investment routes, and a total of 273 paths in 95 countries. This is not a law or a consular list. It is a summary, and the platform itself states that the thresholds fluctuate and need to be verified before applying.

In its ranking, the lowest declared income is from Albania. Unique Permit for digital mobile workers, article 68 of law 79/2021: around $4,845 per year, 12 months with extensions, duration around 84 days, fee about $57. The link to the regulator in the card is unconfirmed. Other trackers for 2026 give a significantly different threshold: around €815 per month, closer to €9,800 per year, or a one-time amount of 408,000 leks based on a 2023 reference without a recent amendment found. A two-fold difference. For the post, this is more important than just the number. Albania is only inexpensive in one database.

The discrepancies are less pronounced in other cases. Ecuador, Visa Nómada based on rentista: around $17,352 per year, which amounts to $1,446 per month, three local minimum wages at $482 each. Duration is 24 months, registry fee about $300, while on other summaries it is $400-450. The country uses the dollar, the threshold is not affected by the exchange rate. There is a path to permanent residency after 21 months, but it is no longer a nomad visa, rather a separate residency requirement.

Brazil, VITEM XIV: from $18,000 per year or $1,500 per month, or this amount in the account. The duration is 12 months with an extension up to 24, processing takes about 15 days, fee around $136. Here, the registry has a link to an official source, and neighboring summaries confirm the figure. The condition is stricter for the money: remote work for a foreign company, not a local contract.

For comparison, consider a typical European route. In 2026, Spain requires 200% of the minimum wage. SMI - €1,221 per month. This equates to about €2,849 per month, or €34,188 per year per person. The first family member adds 75% of SMI, each subsequent member adds 25%. Greece asks for €3,500 net, not gross. UAE for virtual work - about $3,500 per month. The Thai DTV is not based on a salary but on the remaining amount from 500,000 baht.

A significant shift this year is not in the threshold but in the closed door. As of June 30, 2026, Canada is not accepting new applications for the Start-Up Visa. This is a different category, founder-based, but it fell off the map just when nomad lists started to look stable.

The practical conclusion from the registry is brief. A low figure in the aggregator is a reason to review the law, not to buy a ticket. Albania exemplifies this better than anyone: one database gives $4,845 per year, the other provides almost twice as much, and neither can replace a consular certificate on the day of application.

The Aid Worker and the Parade

Four drone strikes hit Gaza on Sunday, according to local journalists, leaving at least two people dead and 16 wounded. 

Gaza sources named one of the dead as Saqr Nabil Musa Qaisi, the Gaza representative of the Turkish aid organization Deniz Feneri, after a car was struck near Deir al-Balah. Initial Palestinian accounts put the wounded total from that strike anywhere between one and 10. 

Israel later said Qaisi was a Hamas Nukhba Force operative who took part in the October 7 assault and had recently worked to attack Israeli troops and civilians and rebuild Hamas capabilities. 

The IDF said he also ran Deniz Feneri’s Gaza operation, alleging that the Turkish charity employed Hamas operatives and financed them. Deniz Feneri presented Qaisi as its humanitarian-aid coordinator. 

The car bombing therefore arrived with two biographies attached: Turkey’s aid worker and Israel’s October 7 operative. 

The organization sits close enough to Ankara for the politics to be obvious. Deniz Feneri has hosted Hamas figures Khaled Mashaal and Sami Abu Zuhri at its gatherings, and Qaisi was known locally as an imam who preached in mosques across southern Gaza. 

Turkey calls this solidarity. Israel calls it a Hamas funding channel. Either way, another Turkish-linked institution has become part of the Gaza battlefield. 

Elsewhere, Gaza sources reported the killing of municipal employee Muadh Abu Nseira near Hamad City in Khan Younis, four wounded in Beit Lahiya, two in al-Salatin and three injured in Jabalia. 

Figures remain fragmented because the attacks, casualty reporting and claims of responsibility are moving faster than verification. 

In Rafah, the anti-Hamas Popular Forces militia under Ghassan al-Dahini released video of dozens of armed men marching under the title “Spear Force.” 

The group says it is expanding recruitment and is thought to field roughly 600 to 800 fighters, making it the largest armed faction openly operating against Hamas inside Gaza. A militia parade is not a victory over Hamas. It is a recruitment commercial filmed inside a war zone.

The drone killed a man described as both aid official and Nukhba fighter. The militia marched to advertise its men. 

Gaza now has humanitarian logos, Hamas cells and anti-Hamas uniforms sharing the same terrain. Every side calls it protection. Every side needs more bodies.

🔔 South Korea targets November review for second stage crypto legislation 

🌐 South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has set November for a National Assembly subcommittee review of the Digital Asset Framework Act, rejecting claims that work on the country’s second stage crypto legislation has been delayed. According to Seo Na yoon, head of the FSC’s virtual asset division, the regulator and lawmakers are moving in the same direction on legislation covering digital asset issuance and distribution, including stablecoins. Speaking at a National Assembly seminar in Seoul on Sept. 22, Seo said differences remain over when the government will submit its draft, but the November review remains part of the planned timetable. 

⚡️ “The FSC is not dragging its feet at all. We share the same view,” Seo said, responding to criticism over the pace of the legislation. “The direction has already been set, and while detailed discussions may be necessary in the process, there is certainly no intention on the FSC’s part to delay.”

🔗 Seo said the regulator wants the legislation passed quickly and expects discussions to proceed using bills that lawmakers have already introduced alongside the government’s proposal. Ten digital asset and stablecoin bills are currently pending in the National Assembly, giving lawmakers existing proposals to work from before the government completes its version.

📌 WHAT ARE TRADING EXIT CYCLES?

When funds are allocated to AI Trading, they are actively involved in the trading process.

Because of this, removing capital from trading is handled through trading exit cycles.

The system offers several options depending on the selected exit timeframe.

Trading exit options:

Fastest exit option
10% commission

2 days
5% commission

4 days
3% commission

6 days
2% commission

10 days
0% commission

The principle is simple:

Faster exit option = higher commission
Longer exit period = lower commission

Why?

The more time the system has to complete the trading exit, the lower the commission for removing funds from active trading.

What does “Instant Withdrawal” mean in the Trading Wallet?

You may currently see the fastest option displayed as Instant Withdrawal with a 10% commission.

This is the fastest available trading exit option, but it should not be understood as a guaranteed instant withdrawal.

Processing still requires time and is not guaranteed to be immediate.

It also does not mean that funds will instantly arrive in your external crypto wallet.

After the trading exit is completed, the funds first become available for withdrawal.

Only then can you submit a separate withdrawal request to your external wallet.
